published_statement: Sec. IV.C (src 3083-3095): 'Our above result, (72), applies generally for non-minimally coupled scalar fields in a curved background smeared over a smooth sampling domain. It is also useful for us to discuss this bound in n-dimensional Minkowski spacetime and make comparisons to the DSNEC proven in [14]. As discussed above, we can equivalently view this as a bound on "improved stress tensors" in a free massive scalar field theory. We will, as usual in this context, renormalize with the Minkowski vacuum state as the reference Hadamard state. Note that while the expression of the null energy operator remains unchanged with the introduction of a mass, the vacuum state psi_0 changes from massless to massive Minkowski vacuum.' Then (75) INT_Sigma f^2 <:T_mn l^m l^n:>_psi >= -2 INT_D d^n alpha/(2pi)^n ((Q x Q)W_0)_kappa(fbar_alpha,f_alpha) - xi INT <:phi^2:>_psi nabla_m nabla_n(l^m l^n f^2); (76) f(x+,x-,y)^2 = f(x+,x-)^2 delta^(n-2)(y); (77)-(78) boosted domains D_eta; after (78): 'the state-dependent term, <:phi^2:>_psi, prevents one from writing down a DSNEC in its standard form a la [14] ... We can make progress if we focus on the class of states obeying <:phi^2:>_psi <= phi_max^2 (79)'; (80) the bound with -|xi| phi_max^2 INT d^2x d_-^2(f^2); (81)-(83) massless, factorised |f~|^2, even n (position space); (84)-(87) delta-scaling, N~_n[gamma, xi, phi~_max^2]; (88)-(89) 'we recover ANEC for any coupling in Minkowski spacetime'. Sec. IV.D: (90) delta+ -> 0, delta+ delta- -> l_UV^2, factorised f; (91) SNEC; (92) Penrose-theorem form; (93) massless SNEC with p_n = 4(n-2)^-1 pi^(-n/2) Gamma((n-2)/2)^-1; (94)-(97) Q_0 = l_UV^-n (p_n/2 + 2|xi| phi~_max^2), Q_2 = l_UV^-(n-4) (p_n/2 + 2|xi| phi~_max^2).
published_hypotheses: n-dimensional MINKOWSKI spacetime (Sec. IV.C first paragraph, src 3086-3087) -- not a curved background
reference Hadamard state = the Minkowski vacuum (massive or massless as appropriate) (src 3089-3095); left sides are normal-ordered <:T:>_psi
free (massive or massless) scalar field, non-minimal coupling xi, viewed as an improved stress tensor (src 3088)
smearing restricted to the two null directions: f^2 = f(x+,x-)^2 delta^(n-2)(y) (76)
momentum domain restricted to boosted half-spaces D_eta (78), eta optimised (80),(82)
state class <:phi^2:>_psi <= phi_max^2 (79), motivated in Sec. V as an EFT field-range cutoff; without it 'a DSNEC in its standard form' cannot be written
(84)-(87): f = F(x+/delta+, x-/delta-)/sqrt(delta+ delta-), INT F^2 = 1, F dropping off quickly
(88)-(89) ANEC: delta+ -> 0, delta- -> infinity, delta+ delta- = alpha^2 fixed, (1/delta+)F^2 -> A delta(x+ - beta)
(90)-(97) SNEC: delta+ -> 0 with delta+ delta- -> l_UV^2 (a UV cutoff), factorised f; (93)-(97) massless; covariant momentum cutoff (k-)max(k+)max << l_UV^-2 or independent bounds (src near (92))

FFKP's (80)-(97) also require the state class (79) <:phi^2:>_psi <= phi_max^2, a free scalar, the null-plane smearing (76), and for (82)-(83),(93)-(97) masslessness and factorisation (81)/(90). Shown by rederive F: with Kretschmann = 0 the tree returns ('EVALUABLE', []) for DSN, although (79) needs a phi_max the tree's own FFKP row marks NOT-FOUND ('HPS print no <phi^2>', qeihps.py:111). This cannot move the actual verdict (REFUSED needs only one failed form hypothesis), but the table over-states the class on which the forms would apply.

ADDED, correctly attributed but transferred in scope: the disjunct 'or sampling << curvature radius' (qeihps.py:120-122, 446) is not in FFKP; it is Kontou 2024 Sec. 3.3 (READ: 'the DSNEC of Equation (49) currently makes sense only on Minkowski spacetime or at length scales sufficiently smaller than the curvature scale'). Kontou's Eq. (49) is the MINIMALLY coupled DSNEC of FFK 2111.05772 ([8] there); the tree applies the sentence to FFKP's NON-minimally coupled forms. The transfer is reasonable -- FFKP's (75)-(97) are derived by the same Minkowski route 'a la [14]' -- but it is a transfer, not a quotation about (75)-(93).

ADDED premise (named in the code, not in either source): the tree operationalises 'sufficiently smaller than the curvature scale' as 'curvature radius > 1 l_P' (qeihps.py:446 label '(>= l_P)', predicate 'min(radii) > 1'), i.e. a sampling length must not be sub-Planckian. Neither FFKP nor Kontou states a Planck floor; it is the semiclassical-validity condition Freivogel-Krommydas 1807.03808 states ('the curvature scales are far from the Planck scale', line 603) and the l_UV cutoff of FFKP's own SNEC (90)-(91). The docstring (qeihps.py:122-124, 131-132) states the conclusion 'sub-Planckian ... REFUSED' without listing this premise among the hypotheses; the code row does. The predicate is LENIENT (> 1 l_P, not >> 1 l_P), so it errs against refusal, and HPS's radii (0.0243, 0.0172 l_P) fail it by a factor ~41-58.

WORDING: qeihps.py:119-120 cites 'reference state: the Minkowski vacuum, eq. (75)'. At source the Minkowski-vacuum choice is the sentence immediately before (75) (src 3089), and (75) as printed is (72) restated with the general symbols (Sigma, dvol, W_0); the attribution is correct in content, located one sentence early.

In Minkowski the difference against the Minkowski vacuum is the standard renormalised <T> (vacuum <T> = 0), so on its own domain the form is de facto absolute; on HPS the Minkowski vacuum is not a state at all. rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (21 checks). A: (94) int f'^2 <= ||f||^2/(2 l^2) + (l^2/2)||f''||^2 holds (Gaussians sigma = 1/2, 1, 3 symbolically, minimum over l of the gap > 0; compact C-infinity bump numerically over l in [0.01,100]). B: (96) Q_0 = (p_n/2 + 2|xi|phi~^2)/l_UV^n and Q_2 = (p_n/2 + 2|xi|phi~^2)/l_UV^(n-4) re-derived exactly from (93) + (94) + triangle inequality + (97) with eps = (2 l_UV^2)^-1; p_4 = 2/pi^2. C: TEXT-LAYER DISCREPANCY -- as extracted, (80)/(85)/(93) print the xi term as INT d_-^2(f^2) with no absolute-value bars, and that integral is identically 0 for rapidly decaying f (sympy: 0 for a Gaussian; numeric -2.8e-13 for a bump, whereas INT|d_-^2(f^2)| = 1.035); (96)'s 2|xi|phi~^2 contributions and the stated use of the triangle inequality on |f||f''| require |d_-^2(f^2)|, so the PDF presumably carries bars the text layer lost. Likewise (79) as extracted is one-sided (<:phi^2:> <= phi_max^2) while the step to (80) needs |<:phi^2:>| <= phi_max^2 because d_-^2(f^2) changes sign. Both RECORDED as discrepancies of the text layer, not errors of FFKP (PDF / SciPost version unread; fluctuation.py precedent). D: ANEC limit (88)-(89): with delta+ delta- = alpha^2 fixed the first term of (85) goes as delta+/(A alpha^n) (agrees with the paper) and the second as C|xi|phi_max^2 delta+/(A alpha^2) = C|xi|phi~^2 delta+/(A alpha^n); the printed 'delta+/(A alpha^4)' matches only at n = 4 in the phi~ form -- a minor printed-power discrepancy that does not affect (89): both terms vanish as delta+ -> 0. E: r_c = 0.0242789 and Kretschmann radius 0.0171677 l_P reproduced to printed precision; K = 4/r_0^4 exactly when r' = r'' = 0 and Phi'' + Phi'^2 = 0 at the throat, and K >= 4/r_0^4 at any throat. F: the tree's DSN verdict on HPS is REFUSED (imported read-only); the flat control returns EVALUABLE with no inputs (the dropped-(79) drift). NOT checked here: the constants N_n[gamma] and P_n (they are given only by reference to [14]); the derivation of (77)-(78) from (75) 'using the results of Ref. [14]'.

lacked_data: FFKP (75)-(97) are theorems about a free scalar in Minkowski spacetime; they rest on no measured datum, so there is no datum the authors lacked that could move them. What was lacking in 2023 -- and, on the evidence READ, is still lacking in 2024 (Kontou 2405.05963 Sec. 3.3: 'This work has not been done yet') and May 2026 (Fliss 2605.18964: flat restatement only) -- is a CALCULATION, not data: a curved-spacetime DSNEC (FFK 2111.05772 p.27 names the route: Hadamard-parametrix renormalisation, perturbative in curvature). Would having it change the tree's conclusion? Evidence either way: (for M) a curved DSNEC could in principle apply at HPS's throat, so the refusal is contingent on the state of the art, not a no-go; (against) any perturbative-in-curvature DSNEC would be controlled by sampling/curvature-radius ratios, and HPS's curvature radius is 0.0243 l_P (Kretschmann radius <= r_0/sqrt2 at ANY throat, rederive E), so the sampling scale would be sub-Planckian, outside the semiclassical regime Freivogel-Krommydas require ('curvature scales far from the Planck scale'). The refusal on HPS therefore does not rest on missing data; it rests on (i) the forms' Minkowski domain, READ at source, and (ii) the tree's named semiclassical premise.
grade_evidence: The tree's central claim STANDS at source: FFKP Sec. IV.C says 'discuss this bound in n-dimensional Minkowski spacetime' and 'renormalize with the Minkowski vacuum state as the reference Hadamard state' (src 3086-3095), and FFK 2111.05772, Kontou 2024 and Fliss 2026 all confirm no curved DSNEC exists; so qeihps.DSNEC_ON_HPS = REFUSED is correct and unaffected. The grade is NARROWED (not STANDS) by the rubric's 'a hypothesis the tree drops': the tree's DSN row carries only {flat} (qeihps.py:405, 446-449), dropping FFKP's state class (79) <:phi^2:> <= phi_max^2 (without which FFKP say no DSNEC in standard form can be written), the free-scalar and null-plane smearing hypotheses, and the massless/factorisation hypotheses of (82)-(83),(93)-(97); rederive F shows the flat control would return EVALUABLE with no inputs. The 'sampling << curvature radius' disjunct is Kontou's sentence about the minimally coupled DSNEC, transferred to FFKP's NMC forms, and the Planck floor is the tree's own (code-named) semiclassical premise. Re-derivation: (94) and (96) re-derived exactly; the ANEC limit (89) holds; two text-layer discrepancies (missing |.| in the xi term, one-sided (79)) and one printed-power discrepancy (alpha^4 vs alpha^n) are RECORDED, not errors -- the PDF was not re-readable this stage. Nothing here refutes FFKP; nothing moves the REFUSED verdict.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the DSN row in qeihps.py lists (79) (phi_max, marked NOT-FOUND on HPS as the FFKP row already does) and the free-scalar/null-smearing hypotheses beside 'flat', and names the Planck floor as a hypothesis in the docstring's statement. To OPEN on the text-layer items: reading the FFKP PDF or SciPost Phys. 16 (2024) 119 to see whether (79)/(80)/(93) carry |.| bars and whether (88)'s power is alpha^4 or alpha^n (any outcome is a discrepancy note, not a grade move for the tree's use). Against the tree's refusal: a published curved-spacetime DSNEC valid for sampling lengths comparable to or above a sub-Planckian curvature radius -- none found in the READ literature through May 2026, and the one later-literature search this stage was refused by quota.
